hypotheses.title: Single Syndicate Common Operator (Arctic Drainer Group)
hypotheses.description: Both eth-recovery-claim.top and claim-revoke-portal.link are directly owned and operated by the same organized threat group, maintaining unified control over infrastructure migration, DNS, and settlement wallets.
supportingObservations: Both portals route victim token approvals to the exact same contract (0x71c8...b82).
Identical nameservers (ns1.offshore-dns.is) reused during host rotation.
Identical Google Analytics tag G-99X4K21Z maintained across migrations.
Exact DOM hash match and custom @arctic_drain_support contact handle.
conditionsToStrengthen: Discovery of registrar account or payment correlation linking NameSilo and Nicenic registrations.
Extraction of private admin keys or API tokens in server configs.
conditionsToWeaken: Evidence that 0x71c8...b82 is an open public factory contract utilized by hundreds of distinct unrelated phishing gangs.
Public GitHub leak of the exact template including the G-99X4K21Z tag.
conditionsToResolve: Proof that smart contract split includes a DaaS platform cut forwarding to an external operator.

hypotheses.title: Syndicated Drainer-as-a-Service (DaaS) Customer Cluster
hypotheses.description: The domains represent distinct independent cybercrime affiliates who both purchase turnkey phishing kit instances from a common DaaS vendor who provides the template and default contracts.
supportingObservations: CryptoDrainer-X v2.4 kit is known to be traded on darknet forums.
contradictingObservations: The exact same intermediate contract and final treasury wallet receive 100% of proceeds without standard 20% affiliate split events.
Domain rotation occurred within 4 hours of the first domain being taken down, showing coordinated continuity.
conditionsToStrengthen: Identification of other unrelated campaigns sending proceeds to different wallets with the same template.
conditionsToWeaken: Exclusive financial funneling to 0x3a4f... aggregator wallet.

hypotheses.title: Shared Bulletproof Hosting Co-Tenancy
hypotheses.description: The IP addresses (185.193.127.44 and 194.26.29.112) are general-purpose offshore proxy hosts, and any other domains observed on these IPs may be coincidental neighbor websites.
supportingObservations: FlyHosting and Alexhost are commercial bulletproof providers hosting hundreds of unrelated grey/black hat services.
Passive DNS shows 80+ other active hostnames mapped to 185.193.127.44.
contradictingObservations: The Arctic Drainer operation specifically migrated between these two distinct ASNs, maintaining identical nameserver setup.
conditionsToStrengthen: Reverse IP enumeration showing e-commerce or gaming sites on the same IP.
conditionsToWeaken: Finding that all other hostnames on 185.193.127.44 belong to the same wildcard cert.
conditionsToResolve: Host server header fingerprinting or TLS handshake fingerprint comparison.
